details: A specialized accelerator for computer-vision workloads, optimized for inference at the edge — e.g. Intel Movidius — sitting alongside GPUs and TPUs in the AI hardware landscape.

explainer.lead: A vision processing unit is a specialized accelerator for computer-vision workloads, optimized for inference at the edge. It matters as a distinct option alongside GPUs and TPUs in the AI hardware landscape.

tiers.eli5: It's a small chip built just for seeing-and-recognizing jobs, so devices can do them without sending everything to a big computer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy VPUs for edge inference, for example Intel Movidius, where performance per watt is the priority. A pitfall is expecting GPU-style capabilities: VPUs emphasize low-precision fixed-point arithmetic and differ from GPUs, which are specialized for video encoding and decoding and for rasterization and texture mapping.
tiers.paperLevel: A VPU is an emerging class of microprocessor, a specific type of AI accelerator designed to accelerate machine vision tasks such as CNN and SIFT. It may include direct camera interfaces and emphasizes on-chip dataflow among many parallel execution units with scratchpad memory, like a spatial architecture or manycore DSP, and low-precision fixed-point arithmetic; VPUs are optimized for performance per watt.

explainer.example: An edge device uses an Intel Movidius VPU to run a CNN vision model locally rather than sending camera data off-chip.
